newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bond markets see rollercoaster day.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bond markets see rollercoaster day.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond markets took investors on a rollercoaster ride on Wednesday, opening the day generally weaker, but recovering most of their losses by the close, traders said.
Corporate bond players noted the markets were unsettled in the morning in anticipation of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony on Capital Hill in the afternoon.
In the high-yield market, recent selling by certain large mutual funds, triggered by cash-outflows from institutional investors, added to the negative sentiment, traders said.
Recently-priced junk bond issues bore the brunt of the morning selling, creating a treacherous envirnment for serveral issuers who were in the market with new deals on Wednesday.
"When the market gets weak, the first bonds you tend to sell are those you don't know as well," said one high-yield manager. "That's why new supply got hit today."

As of Wednesday evening, Sinclair Broadcasting's $200 million 144a high-yield trust preferred deal and ICG Communications' 144a offering of $100 million in zero coupon bonds and $100 in exchageable preferred stock, were still not completed.
Morning selling forced prices down one-half a point across the junk bond market, with new issues being hit the hardest, traders said.
But selling tappered off by midday, traders said. The overall market closed unchanged to one-quarter of a point weaker than yesterday's close, they reported.

An improving market also helped Sun International Hotels Ltd to complete a $200 million 144a offering of 10-year senior subordinated notes via Bear Stearn's & Co Inc late in the day. Nevertheless, the notes priced on the wide end of price talk at 9.07 percent or 250 basis points over Treasuries.
Prices of investment-grade bonds were also hammered in the morning as investors feared follow-through selling on a bid list of $1.44 billion corporate bonds sold on Tuesday.
When that selling did not materialize, bids reemerged, traders reported.
But spreads on high-grade bonds ended the day one basis point wider on average, with longer-maturity issues widening by two to three basis points, traders said.
One trader claimed weakness among emerging market bonds, which has been a drag on the high-yield market this week, was also causing some concern among high-grade investors.
The trader said high-grade corporate bonds could eventually benefit from emerging market weakness, if a protracted drop triggered a "flight-to-qualty" response among investors.

In credit-specific news, long-maturity bonds of News Corp ended the day five basis points wider as a result of press reports that the cable industry was preparing to mount a lobbying campaign to block its efforts to allow Direct Broadcast Satellite providers to carry local channels, traders said.
The abilty to offer local channels is a key part of News Corp's strategy to compete with cable television providers as well as other DBS company, the company has said.
News Corp recently acquired 50 percent of EchoStar Communications Corp, a DBS company.
In other markets, Treasuries and stockss ended the day higher.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at 6945.85, up 93.13 points.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury rose 17/32 to 97-14/32 to yield 6.83 percent.
-Douglas Brown, 212-859-1662
